requirements.summary: useradd datauser created uid=1000/gid=1000 account, confirmed via id command both immediately after creation and post-reboot.

requirements.requirement: /srv/data exists and is owned by datauser
requirements.summary: mkdir /srv/data, chown datauser:datauser, chmod 700 applied; ls -ld confirms ownership/mode both before and after the reboot.

requirements.requirement: datauser limited to 100 MB of storage under /srv/data
requirements.summary: XFS project 'datauser' (project id 1000) bound to /srv/data via /etc/projects and /etc/projid; bhard=bsoft=100m applied and confirmed by xfs_quota report showing datauser 100M/100M limits.

requirements.requirement: Limit enforced by the filesystem itself (kernel-level, not application logic)
requirements.summary: As datauser, a 50MB write under the limit succeeded, and a subsequent write was rejected by the kernel with 'No space left on device' exactly at 100M used (per xfs_quota report), demonstrated both before the reboot and again with a fresh 150MB write after the reboot, confirming XFS project-quota enforcement rather than an application-level check.

requirements.requirement: Required reboot to activate XFS project-quota accounting on root fs, with restart bounded and system healthy afterward
requirements.summary: Pre-restart baseline (boot_id 6aa805ba..., root mounted noquota) captured, live remount confirmed pquota cannot be activated without a reboot, reboot acknowledged before disconnect, polling showed transient connection loss, and post-restart boot_id (bb8b927c...) differed from baseline and matches the fixed after_executor snapshot cross-check. Root filesystem came back mounted with prjquota, and /srv/data, datauser, and quota enforcement were all verified intact/functioning after the restart.

overall_summary: The executor satisfied all material outcomes of the task: datauser was created, /srv/data was created and owned by datauser, and a 100MB limit was enforced via XFS project quota bound to /srv/data. Enforcement was directly demonstrated at the kernel level (ENOSPC at exactly 100M) both before and after a reboot that was required to activate prjquota accounting on the root filesystem. The mandatory node-restart evidence protocol was executed coherently and cross-checks against the fixed before/after boot-identity snapshots. No unnecessary or unreverted mutations were found; final state is clean with /srv/data empty and quota configuration persisted.
limitations: The reboot serves dual purpose (technical requirement to activate XFS pquota and the mandatory restart-evidence protocol); evidence for the two is intertwined rather than cleanly separable, though both aspects are directly observed.

Quota is enforced at the root filesystem level via XFS project quota bound to the /srv/data path rather than via a dedicated mount point for /srv/data; this is a standard and valid XFS approach for directory-level quotas without a separate partition.

operational_hygiene.summary: All mutating commands map clearly to task prerequisites (grubby rootflags=pquota, fstab pquota edit, useradd/mkdir/chown/chmod, XFS project registration and limit-set) or bounded, fully-reverted verification writes (50MB/100MB and 150MB test files removed immediately after each check, confirmed empty by the final ls -la /srv/data). The live remount attempt (cmd-322ed297ed9f44f1) was a legitimate diagnostic that did not alter durable state (mount stayed noquota) and served to justify the reboot. No unnecessary packages were installed, no security controls were weakened, and listening sockets/failed-services were unchanged aside from expected reboot-related PID churn.
